audit.whatIsWrong: Lane-difficulty text described the level-3 stage as swinging to Galio while both level charts (content win[2] and full phases[2].side) say Gragas — an internal contradiction the reader sees on one page.
audit.why: Body Slam is a 600-range stun on a 14s rank-1 cooldown; Shield of Durand slows Galio while it charges (Riot text: 'charges a defensive stance, moving slowly'), so Gragas dictates whether the taunt ever lands. Gragas edges levels 2-3, which is what the charts say.
audit.corrected: Level-3 why now states Gragas's edge (his stun beats the slow W charge) and gives the answer (bait Body Slam first), so text and chart agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Power-spike lines never carried a single cooldown number and referred to Gragas's ult only as 'R knockback'.
audit.why: Galio's Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s with 4000-5500 range; Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s and local. That asymmetry is the whole reason the level-6 spike is Galio's, and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike now contrasts a global R against a 100s local cask; first-item spike names the Rylai's Body Slam into Explosive Cask pick threat plus the Happy Hour anti-heal timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Gragas ability was named (flagged in the packet defects). The text called Barrel Roll a 'Q-pool', called Drunken Rage 'W damage reduction' with no timing, and never mentioned Happy Hour.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is a thrown cask that explodes on activation or after 4 seconds, not a persistent pool. Drunken Rage samples for 1 second and the damage reduction only applies AFTER the sip finishes — that 1 second is the exact window for the taunt release. Happy Hour heals on every skill cast, which is the anti-heal trigger flagged in _missing-interactions.json.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named (Happy Hour, Barrel Roll, Drunken Rage, Body Slam, Explosive Cask); the taunt is now keyed to the 1-second Drunken Rage sip before its reduction turns on; Oblivion Orb tied to Happy Hour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldown section said 'track it before every punch' with no numbers.
audit.why: Body Slam 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 vs Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7 — Galio's dash returns roughly three seconds before Gragas's at rank 1. That is the punishable window and it was never quantified.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block, do's line and Key Ability Interactions all now carry 14s vs 11s and the 18s W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said 'his healing fights your trade math' without naming the source.
audit.why: The heal is Happy Hour, which triggers on every skill cast, not on autos — so Oblivion Orb matters even in a pure poke lane.
audit.corrected: Oblivion Orb line now names Happy Hour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing recorded that Barrel Roll's damage ramps with time before detonation.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'The potency of the explosion increases over time.' Stepping off the cask early is a concrete damage reduction, not a vague 'dodge it'.
audit.corrected: Not written to the page this pass — exact ramp figures are not in the kit file, so only the named-cask correction shipped.

edits.after: With Q-W-E up, start Shield of Durand as Body Slam connects so the magic-amped reduction blanks the Barrel Roll cask, then release the taunt into Justice Punch — his dash is 14s at rank 1, so he has no second exit.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are roughly even — you both have only a piece of your kit and neither wants to commit yet. His real threat is a max-range E body-slam into Q-pool before your W taunt is up, so respect that gap-close and don't sit at half HP in his Q range. The lane swings your way at 3: once Shield of Durand and Justice Punch are online, his AP poke is exactly the damage your W soaks hardest, so bait the body-slam, channel W into his commit, release the taunt, and E-knockup him while he has no second dash to peel out.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are roughly even — you both have one piece of your kit and neither wants to commit. His real threat is a 600-range Body Slam stun into a point-blank Barrel Roll before Shield of Durand is up, so respect that gap-close and don't sit at half HP inside his 850 range. At 3 you get an answer: his AP is exactly what your W soaks hardest, so bait Body Slam, start the charge as it lands, release the taunt inside his 1-second Drunken Rage sip before that reduction turns on, and Justice Punch the knockup while his 14s dash is gone.

edits.before: This is your comfiest stretch, but it stays close. Every time he E's in you have a clean answer — channel Shield of Durand into the magic-amped reduction window, release the taunt, and his Q-pool plus empowered auto do a fraction of their damage while your E-knockup interrupts him. The real lever is 6: Hero's Entrance means you don't have to win the 1v1 to win the matchup — shove and R to a fighting lane, because even-in-lane plus a global is ahead overall. Just watch his W reduction soaking your taunt combo and his R knockback flipping you off your E.
edits.after: This is your comfiest stretch, but it stays close. Every time Body Slam comes in you have a clean answer — charge Shield of Durand into the magic-amped reduction window, release the taunt, and his Barrel Roll plus Drunken Rage auto land for a fraction while Justice Punch knocks him up. The real lever is 6: Hero's Entrance means you don't have to win the 1v1 to win the matchup — shove and R to a fighting lane, because even-in-lane plus a global is ahead overall. Watch a finished Drunken Rage soaking your taunt and Explosive Cask flipping you off your E.

edits.before: It flattens back toward even and can tip his way around items. You're not out-dueling him 1v1, so your late value is your identity: R presence to swing other fights, peeling your carries off his dive, and channeling W to neutralize his AP burst in teamfights rather than trying to splitpush him.
edits.after: It flattens back toward even and can tip his way around items. Once he has Rylai's, Body Slam into Explosive Cask is a genuine pick threat — he flips you under his tower or peels your engage in a fight. You're not out-dueling him 1v1, so your late value is your identity: R presence to swing other fights, peeling your carries off his dive, Grievous Wounds against Happy Hour, and charging W to eat his AP burst in teamfights rather than trying to splitpush him.

notes: Justice Punch carries a derived 'terrain' flag in champ-data/_kits/galio.json; Riot's own description is only a backstep-and-charge knockup with no wall creation, so the flag is a tooltip-parse misfire. _missing-interactions.json builds a 'Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch (E)' headline off that flag for gragas/heimerdinger/karma/kayle — I did not write that claim to any page. Data mismatch worth a look: the scratchpad packet lists galio-vs-gragas at 48.98% over 49 games, while MC_WR_TABLES/MC_REAL_GAMES on disk say 46.81% over 423 games; I treated the on-disk 46.81% as the headline figure per point 1.
